channel.title: Molecular & Cell Biology Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Nature Cell Biology, Genome Biology, Genome Research, and Molecular Cell.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Of rigor and outreach, and practicing what we teach
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01914-y Aditi U. Gurkar is an associate professor at the Aging Institute of the University of Pittsburgh, studying the mechanisms of ageing. We reached out to Aditi to discuss her career, perspective on the cellular ageing field, outreach efforts, and how to practice what we teach when it comes to longevity-promoting practices.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Emerging mechanisms of genome degradation during the mtDNA life cycle
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01903-1 Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is not static but undergoes a regulated ‘life cycle’ that encompasses replication, maintenance, spatial distribution and turnover. Here, we update emerging mtDNA degradative pathways, discuss the interplay between mtDNA quality control and heteroplasmy, and outline crucial questions that place the mtDNA life cycle at the forefront of mitochondrial biology.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: An SP110–SP100 axis is a critical regulator of promyelocytic leukaemia body dynamics and mitotic fidelity
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01916-w Aird et al. report that promyelocytic leukaemia (PML)-localized speckled protein 110 (SP110) controls SP100 oligomerization, which then regulates the mitotic dissolution of nuclear PML bodies.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Time-resolved functional genomics using deep learning reveals global hierarchical control of autophagy
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-025-01837-0 Chica et al. combined genetic network mapping, time-resolved imaging and deep learning to generate a dataset called AutoDRY that describes multilayered control of autophagy and uncovers new regulatory pathways.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Riboflavin metabolism shapes FSP1-driven ferroptosis resistance
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-025-01856-x After performing a focused CRISPR–Cas9 screen, Skafar et al. identify riboflavin (vitamin B2) as a regulator of FSP1 stability that modulates phospholipid peroxidation and ferroptosis sensitivity in cancer cells.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Palmitoylation-mediated regulation of KAT2A promotes lung metastasis in breast cancer
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 13 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01913-z Liu et al. report DHHC20-mediated palmitoylation as a key mechanism for regulating KAT2A expression, which plays an essential role in breast cancer lung metastasis.

Molecular Cell: Molecular basis for dual-spacer-guided target cleavage by the TIGR-TasH system
item.description: Yang et al. presented the molecular basis of the TIGR-TasH system, including autonomous precursor tigRNA processing by the Nop domain, tigRNA-dependent dimerization, lysine-triggered dsDNA unzipping, and β-hairpin-mediated recruitment of the HNH nuclease. Engineering Box C mutants enable the rational design of tigRNA-defined nickases for gene editing in mammalian cells.

Nature Cell Biology: Fat bolsters tumours against ferroptosis
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01904-0 Tumour location dictates ferroptosis resistance. A study indicates that peritumoural adipose tissue aids tumours in evading ferroptosis by supplying tryptophan metabolites, including kynurenine and 3-hydroxykynurenine, which block NCOA4-mediated ferritinophagy to lower levels of labile iron and suppress lipid peroxidation.

item.title: Nature Cell Biology: Peritumoural adipose tissue promotes ferroptosis resistance by 3-hydroxykynurenine-mediated suppression of ferritinophagy
item.description: Nature Cell Biology, Published online: 11 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41556-026-01907-x Zhang, Han, Tan, Lu, Ma et al. report that kynurenine derived from peritumoural adipose tissue is hijacked by cancer cells to mediate ferroptosis resistance, a process that could potentially be targeted with immunotherapy to inhibit tumour growth.

Molecular Cell: Accessory subunits of PRC2 mimic H3K27me3 to restrict the spread of Polycomb domains
item.description: Some proteins mimic the repressive mark H3K27me3, but the physiological relevance of this phenomenon was unclear. Agius et al. show that the PRC2 subunits JARID2 and PALI1 mimic H3K27me3 to antagonize PRC2-mediated H3K27me3 deposition, limit Polycomb domain spreading, and enable timely activation of developmental genes in vivo .

item.title: Molecular Cell: Functional landscape of non-canonical open reading frames in coordinating cell fate
item.description: Zhu et al. establish a paradigm of bifunctional RNAs coordinating cell-fate decisions across cellular compartments. Using sORF-seq, they identify lncPRESS1 as an lncRNA that directs SWI/SNF chromatin targeting while acting as an mRNA encoding a microprotein that modulates ciliogenesis, linking nuclear regulation with cytoplasmic signaling during human embryonic development.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Self-clustering of three CBX2 molecules drives PRC2 to promote facultative heterochromatinization of Polycomb target genes
item.description: Ingersoll et al. uncover that approximately three CBX2 molecules drive PRC2 clustering and H3K27me3 deposition in mESCs. This process supports a model in which few CBX2 molecules self-cluster on chromatin, initiating condensate assembly while concurrently recruiting and stabilizing PRC2 at nucleation sites for H3K27me3 deposition and cellular differentiation.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Sequence-specific RNA recognition drives Restrictor-mediated termination of extragenic transcription
item.description: Polizzese et al. show that the C3H1 zinc fingers (ZNFs) of ZC3H4 confer sequence-specific RNA binding to Restrictor. These ZNFs recognize a degenerate A/UGUA motif at ncRNA 5′ ends and are required for termination, whereas tethering of Restrictor to early elongating RNA Pol II depends instead on WDR82.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Global profiling of nascent chain interactors reveals TRIM25 as a co-translational E3 ubiquitin ligase
item.description: Nascent polypeptides emerging from the ribosome engage co-translational factors that assist maturation and quality control to maintain proteostasis. Xiong et al. systematically profiled these factors and identified the major E3 ubiquitin ligase that targets misfolded nascent chains at the ribosome.

Molecular Cell: The human antibacterial factor APOL3 couples lysosomal damage to mitochondrial DNA efflux and type I IFN induction
item.description: Ritacco et al. uncover an immune-inducible pathway that explains how lysosomal damage can trigger inflammation. Priming with the cytokine interferon-γ induces the antibacterial effector protein APOL3, which, upon sensing lysosomal injury, unleashes a membranolytic attack on the cell’s own mitochondria, releasing pro-inflammatory DNA and activating innate immunity.

Molecular Cell: Filament-driven activation of the Kongming antiviral system by deoxyinosine triphosphate
item.description: Recently, the Kongming system has been identified as a bacterial anti-phage defense system relied on nucleobase-modified nucleotides for immune signaling. Zhen et al. determine a series of cryo-EM structures of this system, revealing that dITP binding induces filament assembly of KomBC, which elucidats the activation mechanism of the Kongming system.

item.title: Molecular Cell: Filament-mediated repurposing of toxic dITP for immunity in the Kongming system
item.description: Feng et al. uncover how a bacterial immune effector, KomBC, is activated by the toxic nucleotide dITP. A preassembled filament converts sparse, non-cyclic dITP signals into cooperative NADase activation, revealing a distinct ultrasensitive immune mechanism.
